tables.name: customers
tables.schema: CREATE TABLE customers (customer_id character varying(5), company_name character varying(40), contact_name character varying(30), contact_title character varying(30), city character varying(15), region character varying(15), country character varying(15));
tables.description: Companies that place orders. One row per customer account.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: unique identifier for a customer (5-character code)

columns.name: company_name
columns.description: name of the customer's company

columns.name: contact_name
columns.description: name of the primary contact person at the company

columns.name: city
columns.description: city the customer is located in

columns.name: region
columns.description: state/region the customer is located in

columns.name: country
columns.description: country the customer is located in

sample_queries.query: select count(*) as total_customers from customers where country = 'Germany'
sample_queries.user_input: How many customers do we have in Germany?

sample_queries.query: select country, count(*) as customer_count from customers group by country order by customer_count desc limit 10
sample_queries.user_input: Which countries have the most customers?

tables.name: orders
tables.schema: CREATE TABLE orders (order_id smallint, customer_id character varying(5), employee_id smallint, order_date date, required_date date, shipped_date date, ship_via smallint, freight real, ship_country character varying(15));
tables.description: One row per order placed by a customer. Links to customers, employees, and order_details.

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: unique identifier for an order

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: id of the customer who placed the order

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: id of the employee (sales rep) who handled the order

columns.name: order_date
columns.description: date the order was placed

columns.name: shipped_date
columns.description: date the order was shipped; null if not yet shipped

columns.name: ship_via
columns.description: id of the shipper used for this order, references shippers.shipper_id

columns.name: freight
columns.description: shipping cost for the order

columns.name: ship_country
columns.description: country the order was shipped to

sample_queries.query: select count(*) as order_count from orders where order_date >= '1997-01-01' and order_date < '1998-01-01'
sample_queries.user_input: How many orders were placed in 1997?

sample_queries.query: select count(*) as unshipped_orders from orders where shipped_date is null
sample_queries.user_input: How many orders have not shipped yet?

sample_queries.query: select c.company_name, count(o.order_id) as order_count from orders o join customers c on o.customer_id = c.customer_id group by c.company_name order by order_count desc limit 5
sample_queries.user_input: Which customers have placed the most orders?

tables.name: order_details
tables.schema: CREATE TABLE order_details (order_id smallint, product_id smallint, unit_price real, quantity smallint, discount real);
tables.description: Line items for each order: which products, quantities, and prices. One row per product per order. Revenue for an order is sum(unit_price * quantity * (1 - discount)) across its line items.

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: id of the order this line item belongs to, references orders.order_id

columns.name: product_id
columns.description: id of the product ordered, references products.product_id

columns.name: unit_price
columns.description: price per unit at time of order

columns.name: quantity
columns.description: number of units ordered

columns.name: discount
columns.description: discount applied, as a decimal fraction (e.g. 0.15 = 15% off)

sample_queries.query: select sum(unit_price * quantity * (1 - discount)) as total_revenue from order_details od join orders o on od.order_id = o.order_id where o.order_date >= '1997-01-01' and o.order_date < '1998-01-01'
select p.product_name, sum(od.quantity) as units_sold from order_details od join products p on od.product_id = p.product_id group by p.product_name order by units_sold desc limit 5
sample_queries.user_input: What are the top 5 best-selling products by units sold?

tables.name: products
tables.schema: CREATE TABLE products (product_id smallint, product_name character varying(40), supplier_id smallint, category_id smallint, unit_price real, units_in_stock smallint, discontinued integer);
tables.description: Catalog of items that can be ordered.

columns.name: product_id
columns.description: unique identifier for a product

columns.name: product_name
columns.description: name of the product

columns.name: category_id
columns.description: id of the category this product belongs to, references categories.category_id

columns.name: unit_price
columns.description: list price per unit

columns.name: units_in_stock
columns.description: current inventory count

columns.name: discontinued
columns.description: 1 if the product is discontinued, 0 if active

sample_queries.query: select count(*) as discontinued_count from products where discontinued = 1
select product_name, units_in_stock from products where units_in_stock < reorder_level and discontinued = 0
sample_queries.user_input: Which active products are below their reorder level?

tables.name: categories
tables.schema: CREATE TABLE categories (category_id smallint, category_name character varying(15), description text);
tables.description: Product categories, e.g. Beverages, Condiments, Produce.

columns.name: category_id
columns.description: unique identifier for a category

columns.name: category_name
columns.description: name of the category

sample_queries.query: select cat.category_name, sum(od.quantity) as units_sold from order_details od join products p on od.product_id = p.product_id join categories cat on p.category_id = cat.category_id group by cat.category_name order by units_sold desc
sample_queries.user_input: Which product category sells the most units?

tables.name: employees
tables.schema: CREATE TABLE employees (employee_id smallint, last_name character varying(20), first_name character varying(10), title character varying(30), hire_date date, reports_to smallint);

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: unique identifier for an employee

columns.name: first_name
columns.description: employee's first name

columns.name: last_name
columns.description: employee's last name

columns.name: title
columns.description: employee's job title, e.g. Sales Representative

columns.name: hire_date
columns.description: date the employee was hired

sample_queries.query: select e.first_name, e.last_name, count(o.order_id) as orders_handled from orders o join employees e on o.employee_id = e.employee_id group by e.first_name, e.last_name order by orders_handled desc limit 5
sample_queries.user_input: Which employees have handled the most orders?

tables.name: shippers
tables.schema: CREATE TABLE shippers (shipper_id smallint, company_name character varying(40), phone character varying(24));
tables.description: Shipping companies used to fulfill orders. Referenced by orders.ship_via.

columns.name: shipper_id
columns.description: unique identifier for a shipper

columns.name: company_name
columns.description: name of the shipping company

sample_queries.query: select s.company_name, count(o.order_id) as order_count from orders o join shippers s on o.ship_via = s.shipper_id group by s.company_name order by order_count desc
sample_queries.user_input: How many orders did each shipping company handle?
